legend: Mateo, the owner of Austin's most popular video game store, was in a generous mood one day. He decides to give a gift to each of the n$$$n$$$ people currently in his store and he has n$$$n$$$ distinct prizes labeled 0,1,…,n−1$$$0, 1, \dots, n - 1$$$ to give out. Since Mateo never does anything the simple way, he comes up with the following scheme to give the prizes out.

He gives each of the n$$$n$$$ people in the store unique numbers from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$ (inclusive). He then asks everyone to form a line and so the resulting ordering of the people can be written as the sequence [x1,x2,…,xn]$$$[x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n]$$$ (where each xi$$$x_i$$$ is unique and 1≤xi≤n$$$1 \leq x_i \leq n$$$). The prize which Mateo gives person xj$$$x_j$$$ is equal to x1⋅x2⋅…⋅xj−1⋅xj(modn)$$$x_1 \cdot x_2 \cdot \ldots \cdot x_{j-1} \cdot x_{j} \pmod{n}$$$. Unfortunately, Mateo only has one of each prize so he asks you to come up with an ordering of the n$$$n$$$ people so that each person will get a unique prize number.
input: The first and only line of input will contain a single integer n$$$n$$$ (1≤n≤5⋅105$$$1 \leq n \leq 5 \cdot 10^5$$$), representing the number of people in the store.
output: A space-separated permutation of the numbers from 1$$$1$$$ to n$$$n$$$ (inclusive), representing the ordering of people such that each person can get a distinct prize. Output -1 if there is no such permutation.
note: The product after the first person is 1$$$1$$$ so the first person gets prize 1$$$1$$$.
The product after the second person is 1⋅4=4≡4(mod7)$$$1 \cdot 4 = 4 \equiv 4 \pmod{7}$$$ so the second person gets prize 4$$$4$$$
The product after the third person is 4⋅3=12≡5(mod7)$$$4 \cdot 3 = 12 \equiv 5 \pmod{7}$$$ so the third person gets prize 5$$$5$$$.
The product after the fourth person is 5⋅6=30≡2(mod7)$$$5 \cdot 6 = 30 \equiv 2 \pmod{7}$$$ so the fourth person gets prize 2$$$2$$$.
The product after the fifth person is 5⋅2=10≡3(mod7)$$$5 \cdot 2 = 10 \equiv 3 \pmod{7}$$$ so the fifth person gets prize 3$$$3$$$.
The product after the sixth person is 3⋅2=6≡6(mod7)$$$3 \cdot 2 = 6 \equiv 6 \pmod{7}$$$ so the sixth person gets prize 6$$$6$$$.
The product after the seventh person is 6⋅7=42≡0(mod7)$$$6 \cdot 7 = 42 \equiv 0 \pmod{7}$$$ so the seventh person gets prize 0$$$0$$$.

legend.ai: Mateo 是奥斯汀最受欢迎的视频游戏商店的店主。一天，他心情很好，决定给当时在店里的 n$$$n$$$ 个人每人送一份礼物。他有 n$$$n$$$ 个互不相同的奖品，编号为 0,1,…,n−1$$$0, 1, \dots, n - 1$$$。由于 Mateo 从来不会用最简单的方式做事，他想出了以下发放奖品的方案。

他给店里的 n$$$n$$$ 个人分别编号为 1$$$1$$$ 到 n$$$n$$$(包括两端)。随后，他让所有人排成一列，于是可以将这些人的排列记作序列 [x1,x2,…,xn]$$$[x_1, x_2, \dots, x_n]$$$(其中每个 xi$$$x_i$$$ 都互不相同，且满足 1≤xi≤n$$$1 \leq x_i \leq n$$$)。他给第 j$$$x_j$$$ 个人的奖品编号等于 x1⋅x2⋅…⋅xj−1⋅xj(modn)$$$x_1 \cdot x_2 \cdot \ldots \cdot x_{j-1} \cdot x_{j} \pmod{n}$$$。不幸的是，Mateo 每种奖品只有一份，因此他请你设计一个 n$$$n$$$ 个人的排列，使得每个人得到的奖品编号都互不相同。

input.ai: 输入的第一行(也是唯一一行)包含一个整数 n$$$n$$$(1≤n≤5⋅105$$$1 \leq n \leq 5 \cdot 10^5$$$)，表示店内的人数。

output.ai: 输出一组由空格分隔的数字 1$$$1$$$ 到 n$$$n$$$(含两端)的排列，表示一种能让每个人获得不同奖品的人员顺序。如果不存在这样的排列，则输出 -1。

note.ai: 第一个人处理完后，乘积为 1$$$1$$$，因此第一个人获得奖品 1$$$1$$$。
第二个人处理完后，乘积为 1⋅4=4≡4(mod7)$$$1 \cdot 4 = 4 \equiv 4 \pmod{7}$$$，因此第二个人获得奖品 4$$$4$$$
第三个人处理完后，乘积为 4⋅3=12≡5(mod7)$$$4 \cdot 3 = 12 \equiv 5 \pmod{7}$$$，因此第三个人获得奖品 5$$$5$$$。
第四个人处理完后，乘积为 5⋅6=30≡2(mod7)$$$5 \cdot 6 = 30 \equiv 2 \pmod{7}$$$，因此第四个人获得奖品 2$$$2$$$。
第五个人处理完后，乘积为 5⋅2=10≡3(mod7)$$$5 \cdot 2 = 10 \equiv 3 \pmod{7}$$$，因此第五个人获得奖品 3$$$3$$$。
第六个人处理完后，乘积为 3⋅2=6≡6(mod7)$$$3 \cdot 2 = 6 \equiv 6 \pmod{7}$$$，因此第六个人获得奖品 6$$$6$$$。
第七个人之后的乘积为 6⋅7=42≡0(mod7)$$$6 \cdot 7 = 42 \equiv 0 \pmod{7}$$$，因此第七个人获得奖品 0$$$0$$$。
